checks: Original 6f9d37b455a5cd1c §3 uses the nearest point partition. Relative face interiors and their normal-cone directions give disjoint pieces up to volume-null seams. Their tangent and normal spaces are orthogonal, so the Jacobian factors by product measure.

Uniform strict vertex signs retain the same cap pattern for all shifts of length at most tau. A face missing the positive vertex contributes zero. On an incident k-face its edge intercept ratios multiply to the displayed fraction; the k=0 sector is wholly captured.

For the moving face the normal cone is the inverse-transpose image of the fixed cone. In reference polar coordinates put the radial variable equal to τr/|L_W θ|. Its radial Jacobian yields exactly J_W τ^q|L_W θ|^(−q)r^(q−1).

The fixed spherical cone has finite measure and invertibility keeps its denominators uniformly positive. Finite expansions give powers τ^q through τ^(q+k); smooth coefficients yield the O(τ) convergence of all specified partial derivatives on smaller compact sets.

In the planar case integrate each adjacent strip length with its signed u·n shift over the radius and add the selected vertex sector angle τ²/2. This agrees with both displayed coefficients in §7 (20).

overlap.comparison: Its unrounded fixed-threshold one-vertex formula supplies the zero-radius value. It does not cover rounded face tubes, moving plane parameters, or convergence of the resulting derivatives.

review_method: Independent cold proof read, source and predecessor comparison, and exact computations where applicable.
summary: Orthogonal nearest-face tubes give exact small-radius polynomials for total volume and the one-positive-vertex cap, with joint smooth parameter coefficients and the stated planar constants.
